# the container stays as it is; its systemd scope gets the pseudo terminal rule runc 1.1.3 left out (kept by systemd through every reload)
sudo systemctl set-property --runtime bench73434226-web.scope 'DeviceAllow=char-pts rwm'

L=/var/lib/bench73434226
ROOT=/run/bench73434226/runc
ENG=$L/bin/runc
SCOPE=bench73434226-web.scope
# a restart makes the exec work until the next daemon-reload: the same runc builds the same scope
sudo "$ENG" --root "$ROOT" delete -f web
for _ in $(seq 1 40); do [ "$(systemctl is-active $SCOPE 2>/dev/null)" = active ] || break; sleep 0.5; done
RUNCBIN=$ENG
cd $L/bundle
sudo "$RUNCBIN" --systemd-cgroup --root $ROOT run -d --pid-file /run/bench73434226/web.pid web </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do sudo grep -q "token=" /run/bench73434226/data/heartbeat 2>/dev/null && break; sleep 0.5; done

L=/var/lib/bench73434226
ROOT=/run/bench73434226/runc
ENG=$L/bin/runc
SCOPE=bench73434226-web.scope
# the device node's mode is not what refuses the open: the cgroup's device rules are
sudo chmod 666 /dev/ptmx /dev/pts/* 2>/dev/null || true
sudo "$ENG" --root "$ROOT" exec web /bin/sh -c 'chmod 666 /dev/ptmx /dev/pts/* 2>/dev/null; true' || true

L=/var/lib/bench73434226
ROOT=/run/bench73434226/runc
ENG=$L/bin/runc
SCOPE=bench73434226-web.scope
# a newer runc on the engineer's path: its own exec happens to work, but the container's scope still lacks the rule and every runc 1.1.3 exec still fails
sudo install -m 755 "$(command -v runc)" "$ENG"

c = json.load(open(p))
c["linux"]["resources"]["devices"] = [{"allow": True, "access": "rwm"}]
json.dump(c, open(p, "w"), indent=2)
EOF
sudo "$ENG" --root "$ROOT" delete -f web

EOF
sudo "$ENG" --root "$ROOT" delete -f web
